title: Sky-pooler cutover leaves index-4 unmintable: newPooler._minter never set to NFTMinterV2, mint(4) reverts
description: RECONCILIATION of run-09 M-01 against HEAD 30775401. The script was rewritten to call BalancerPoolerV2(newPooler).setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) at step 6, immediately followed by a hard storage assertion require(vm.load(newPooler, slot1) == NFT_MINTER_V2) and (in preview) an end-to-end mint(4) proof at step 16. The new pooler's ATokenDispatcherV2._minter is now wired to NFTMinterV2, so dispatch()'s onlyMinter gate passes and mint(4) works after the cutover runs alone — no follow-up SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler / FixBalancerPoolerV2SetMinter transaction needed.
impact: RESOLVED. Index-4 minting is functional immediately after the cutover. The availability break reported in run-09 no longer occurs.
evidence: VERIFIED on mainnet fork (block 25242176). (1) Dry preview reaches step 6 and logs 'newPooler._minter (slot1) verified == NFTMinterV2', then step 16 mints one id-4 NFT (balance 0->1, hook mintDebt accrued). (2) PoC-replay: the run-09 reproduction test/AuditSkyPoolerMintIndex4.t.sol::test_mint4_reverts_after_cutover_alone NOW FAILS ('next call did not revert as expected') because mint(4) no longer reverts — the strongest 'fixed' signal under recheck semantics. (3) New PoC test/AuditSkyPoolerMintIndex4_Fixed.t.sol::test_mint4_succeeds_after_cutover_alone_FIXED PASSES: after the cutover alone, slot1==NFT_MINTER_V2 and a fresh USER mints 1 id-4 NFT. (4) slot1==_minter validated independently on BOTH the live pooler (cast storage slot1 == 0x39Af…2e10f) and the freshly-deployed artifact (vm.load post-deploy).
recommendation: No further action required for M-01. The slot1 require is fail-closed and runs on both :dry and :broadcast, so the fix holds even though the e2e mint proof is preview-only. Suggest /ledger marking M-01 fixed.

title: Broadcast uses --skip-simulation with an offline-derived stale-able minBPT; no live re-query enforced
scriptRef: script/DispatcherReplaceSkyPoolerAtIndex4.s.sol:_step17_finalPool (692-770); DEFAULT_MIN_BPT line 109; broadcast cmd package.json line 183
description: RECONCILIATION of run-09 L-01 against HEAD. The broadcast variant still runs --skip-simulation (package.json line 183) and minBPT is still supplied from the offline-derived DEFAULT_MIN_BPT=284e18 (or MIN_BPT_WEI env), with NO live in-script re-query — confirmed unchanged. The router queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced quote still cannot run from a tx frame (NotStaticCall), so the floor remains an offline constant the operator must refresh per the code comment. The seed is read live (partially self-correcting), but the floor is not. The rewrite DID add a mitigation: pool() is now wrapped in try/catch (step 17), so a too-high stale floor that reverts pool() no longer rolls back or strands the already-committed dispatcher cutover — it logs 'LP add DEFERRED', parks the seeded sUSDS recoverably, and the owner re-pools later with a fresh minBPT.
impact: Operational, bounded. The run-09 worst case (a stale-too-high minBPT stranding a half-applied cutover) is now neutralized by the try/catch isolation. Residual: a stale-too-low floor weakens slippage protection on the single LP add (no in-script auto-detection); a stale-too-high floor silently defers the LP add (sUSDS parks un-LP'd until a manual re-pool). Both require pool/seed drift beyond the held margin AND the operator skipping the documented MIN_BPT_WEI re-query.
evidence: FORK-PROVEN (block 25242176). Default run: seed ~527.8 sUSDS (broadcast-equivalent), pool() minted ~287.9 BPT vs 284e18 floor (margin held). Forced MIN_BPT_WEI=1e23: pool() reverts, but the cutover (replaceDispatcher, hook rotation) stays committed, step-16 e2e mint still succeeded, and 'sUSDS held (un-LP'd)' is logged as recoverable — confirming the try/catch isolation works as designed and the cutover is never stranded. Broadcast command still carries --skip-simulation.
recommendation: Before broadcast, re-derive minBPT live via the documented cast queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced for the actual current seed and set MIN_BPT_WEI explicitly; or refuse to broadcast unless MIN_BPT_WEI is supplied for current state. The try/catch mitigation is good but does not remove the stale-floor / weak-slippage residual — recommend keeping L-01 open with a note that the stranding sub-impact is resolved.
